D1 — Review all 7 design dimensions, or focus on specific ones?
Project/branch/task: main — design review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign) against DESIGN.md.
ELI10: I've rated the plan 6/10 on design completeness. Its accepted behavior is thorough, but it lists five places where the proposed form breaks DESIGN.md (Save looks like every other button, three different section gaps, error text at ~3:1 contrast, three label sizes, a 2-5 second Save with no spinner) and leaves them undecided. The review walks 7 passes (info architecture, states, journey, AI-slop, design-system alignment, responsive/a11y, open decisions) and asks you one question per gap. Mockups and outside voices are skipped per your request.
Stakes if we pick wrong: narrowing focus means some of the five known violations ship unresolved; the implementer picks tokens by guess.
Recommendation: A because you asked for all seven and every one of the five gaps maps to a different pass.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Pros / cons:
A) All 7 passes, all five gaps plus any new findings (recommended)
  ✅ Every DESIGN.md violation gets its own decision and a verification step in the plan
  ✅ State table and journey storyboard get written so the implementer builds from a spec
  ❌ Roughly six to eight individual questions before the review report is done
B) Only the five listed gaps (Passes 1, 2, 4, 5); skip journey, responsive, decisions
  ✅ Faster: resolves exactly what PLAN.md already flagged and nothing more
  ✅ Fewer questions if you trust the accepted-behavior section as-is
  ❌ Misses gaps the plan didn't self-report, like how status text plus Retry lay out at 320px
Net: full coverage costs a few extra questions; partial coverage trusts a plan that already self-reports five violations.

D2 — Issue 1 (G1): How should Save be distinguished from Reset, Cancel and Export?
Project/branch/task: main — PLAN.md header action group, Pass 1 Information Architecture.
ELI10: Right now the four header buttons look identical, so a user scanning the page can't tell which one commits their edits. DESIGN.md already decides this: Save is the only filled button (#1d4ed8 with white text, 6.7:1 contrast), and Reset, Cancel and Export are neutral ghost buttons. Nothing else about the buttons changes: same 44px height, same order, same disabled and pending looks.
Stakes if we pick wrong: users hesitate over four equal buttons, or hit Export or Reset when they meant Save; the dirty-state confirmation dialogs then do extra work covering for a hierarchy the header should have carried.
Recommendation: 1A because DESIGN.md already names the tokens and it reuses the existing Button variants with zero new components (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min).
Completeness: 1A=10/10, 1B=7/10, 1C=2/10
Pros / cons:
1A) Apply DESIGN.md: Save filled #1d4ed8/white, the other three neutral ghost buttons (recommended)
  ✅ One primary action visible in the 3-second scan, matching every other form in the app
  ✅ Reuses the existing Button primary and ghost variants; only the header wiring changes
  ❌ Adds a verification step: contrast and pending/disabled looks of the filled variant must be checked
1B) Filled Save, and demote Reset/Cancel/Export to text-style links instead of ghost buttons
  ✅ Stronger contrast between primary and secondary actions than ghost buttons give
  ✅ Still keeps Save first and full-width at 640px and below
  ❌ Deviates from DESIGN.md's ghost-button vocabulary and risks link-shaped controls losing their 44px target look
1C) Leave all four buttons identical; rely on Save being first in order
  ✅ No visual change to ship, so nothing new to verify
  ❌ Keeps the hierarchy violation PLAN.md itself flags; Pass 1 stays at 6/10
Net: 1A is the approved system applied as written; 1B trades consistency for extra contrast; 1C leaves the primary action invisible.

questions.question:
D3 — Issue 2 (G5): What does the user see during the 2-5 second Save request?
Project/branch/task: main — PLAN.md Save button pending state, Pass 2 Interaction States.
ELI10: Today the page just sits there for 2-5 seconds after you press Save, and people press again or assume it broke. The plan already says pending feedback lives on the button (not in the status live region) and already specifies this exact treatment for Export. DESIGN.md's established pattern is an inline spinner beside the text “Saving…” inside the Save button, aria-busy=true, with the spinner replaced by a static indicator when the user prefers reduced motion. Save keeps aria-disabled=true plus the activation guard the plan already describes; InlineStatus text does not change.
Stakes if we pick wrong: double submissions, users navigating away mid-save, or a screen reader hearing nothing for five seconds and the user assuming Save failed.
Recommendation: 2A because it is the existing pattern already used by Export on the same header, so both requests feel identical (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min).
Completeness: 2A=10/10, 2B=6/10, 2C=1/10
Pros / cons:
2A) DESIGN.md pattern: spinner beside “Saving…” inside the aria-disabled Save button, aria-busy=true, reduced-motion fallback (recommended)
  ✅ Matches the Export pending treatment already in the plan, so one pattern covers both requests
  ✅ Screen readers get aria-busy on the focused button without a second announcement in the status region
  ❌ The filled primary needs a pending look that is visibly distinct from its disabled look; must be verified
2B) Full-form skeleton or overlay while Save is pending
  ✅ Impossible to miss that something is happening
  ✅ Blocks edits mid-request, which sidesteps the dirty-during-pending question
  ❌ Hides the user's own values for up to 5 seconds and contradicts “do not move focus while pending” and the preserve-edits rule
2C) No pending indicator; rely on the button being aria-disabled
  ✅ Zero implementation work
  ❌ Sighted users see a frozen page; the gap PLAN.md itself flags stays open
Net: 2A reuses the pattern already specified for Export; 2B is louder but breaks two accepted rules; 2C ships the frozen page.

options.label: 2A Spinner + “Saving…” in Save button (recommended)
options.description: DESIGN.md pending pattern: inline spinner beside “Saving…”, aria-busy=true, reduced-motion fallback. Status text unchanged.

options.label: 2B Form skeleton/overlay while pending
options.description: Replace or cover the form during Save. Contradicts preserve-edits and no-focus-move rules.

options.label: 2C No indicator
options.description: Decline the fix; Save is aria-disabled only. Gap G5 stays open.

questions.question:
D4 — Issue 3 (G4): Which type sizes do form labels and headings use?
Project/branch/task: main — PLAN.md form labels and section headings, Pass 4 AI Slop / type hierarchy.
ELI10: The proposed form uses three label sizes (14, 16, 18px) with no rule for which is which, so the hierarchy reads as accidental, and 14px labels are below the 16px floor for readable form text. DESIGN.md defines two roles: 16px for body, form labels and helper text; 20px for the Profile and Notifications headings. Nothing about the font family changes (system-ui stays, per the accepted scope).
Stakes if we pick wrong: users squint at 14px labels on a phone, and three near-identical sizes make the two h2 headings look no more important than a field label, so the page loses its scan structure.
Recommendation: 3A because it is the approved system, removes the sub-16px text, and gives the h2s a real step up (human: ~30min / CC: ~5min).
Completeness: 3A=10/10, 3B=6/10, 3C=1/10
Pros / cons:
3A) DESIGN.md two roles: 16px labels/helper/body, 20px h2 section headings (recommended)
  ✅ Every label and helper text clears the 16px readability floor on mobile
  ✅ Headings get a visible 4px step, so Profile and Notifications read as sections at a glance
  ❌ Any existing 14px helper text grows; the 320px layout must be rechecked for wrapping
3B) Keep three sizes but raise the floor: 16px helper, 18px labels, 20px headings
  ✅ Clears the 16px floor without collapsing helper and label into one size
  ✅ Preserves a distinct helper-text voice if that is used elsewhere
  ❌ Adds a third role DESIGN.md does not have, and 18px labels next to 20px headings flattens the heading step to 2px
3C) Leave 14/16/18px as proposed
  ✅ No change to ship
  ❌ Keeps sub-16px text and the accidental hierarchy PLAN.md itself flags; Pass 4 stays at 7/10
Net: 3A applies the two-role system as approved; 3B invents a third role and weakens headings; 3C ships small, unstructured type.

options.description: DESIGN.md typography: 16px body, labels and helper; 20px h2 section headings. Font family unchanged.

options.label: 3B Three sizes with 16px floor
options.description: 16px helper, 18px labels, 20px headings. Adds a role DESIGN.md lacks.

D5 — Issue 4 (G2): What vertical spacing scale does the form use?
Project/branch/task: main — PLAN.md section and field spacing, Pass 5 Design System Alignment.
ELI10: The proposed form uses 24px between some sections, 32px between others and 16px in a third place, with no rule behind it, so the gaps look random and the eye can't tell where one section ends. DESIGN.md uses an 8px base: 32px between sections (header to Profile, Profile to Notifications), 24px between field groups inside a section, 8px from a label to its input. Same values apply at 320px.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Profile and Notifications don't read as two sections, a field can look closer to the previous section's last input than to its own label, and every new field an engineer adds picks yet another gap.
Recommendation: 4A because it is the approved scale, it is three numbers, and it is checkable with a ruler (human: ~30min / CC: ~5min).
Completeness: 4A=10/10, 4B=7/10, 4C=1/10
Pros / cons:
4A) DESIGN.md 8px scale: sections 32px, field groups 24px, label-to-input 8px (recommended)
  ✅ Gestalt proximity does the grouping: the largest gap is always a section boundary
  ✅ Three tokens, so a computed-style check can verify every gap in the form
  ❌ Existing hand-tuned margins in the shell get replaced, which needs a visual snapshot check
4B) Keep 32px sections but compress to 16px field groups for a denser form
  ✅ Shorter page on a 320px phone, fewer scrolls to reach Notifications
  ✅ Still gives a clear section boundary at 32px
  ❌ Deviates from DESIGN.md's 24px field-group token; label-to-input 8px vs group 16px is a weak 2:1 step
4C) Leave the mixed 24/32/16px gaps
  ✅ No change to ship
  ❌ Keeps the inconsistency PLAN.md itself flags; Pass 5 cannot pass 7/10
Net: 4A is the approved rhythm; 4B trades one token for density; 4C ships random gaps.

options.description: Sections 32px, field groups 24px, label-to-input 8px, at all widths. Verified by computed styles.

questions.question:
D6 — Issue 5 (G3): How are field and network errors colored and marked?
Project/branch/task: main — PLAN.md error messages (field errors, ErrorSummary, network/Export/read errors), Pass 5 Design System Alignment.
ELI10: The proposed error style is red text on light pink at roughly 3:1 contrast, which fails WCAG AA (4.5:1) for 16px text, so people with low vision or a dim phone screen can't read why their save failed. DESIGN.md's tokens are error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2 (computed 7.6:1, passes AA and AAA), always paired with an icon and explicit text so red is never the only signal. The icon is decorative (aria-hidden) because the text carries the meaning.
Stakes if we pick wrong: the one message a user most needs to read is the hardest one on the page to read, and an audit flags an AA failure on every error state.
Recommendation: 5A because it is the approved token pair, it measures 7.6:1, and it applies to every error surface in the plan with one change (human: ~30min / CC: ~5min).
Completeness: 5A=10/10, 5B=6/10, 5C=1/10
Pros / cons:
5A) DESIGN.md tokens: #991b1b text on #fef2f2 surface, icon (aria-hidden) plus explicit text, on all error surfaces (recommended)
  ✅ 7.6:1 measured contrast clears AA with room for dim screens and night-mode filters
  ✅ One token pair covers field errors, ErrorSummary, network, Export and read failures consistently
  ❌ Any existing lighter red elsewhere in the app now looks off next to this form until it is migrated
5B) Keep the pink surface, darken only the text until it reaches 4.5:1
  ✅ Minimal visual change from the current proposal
  ✅ Passes AA on the number alone
  ❌ Introduces a third red that DESIGN.md does not define, and leaves the icon-plus-text rule unstated
5C) Leave red on pink at ~3:1
  ✅ No change to ship
  ❌ Fails WCAG AA on the message users most need; PLAN.md itself flags it
Net: 5A is the approved pair with measured headroom; 5B fixes the number but forks the palette; 5C ships an AA failure.

options.description: DESIGN.md error tokens (7.6:1) on every error surface; icon aria-hidden, text explicit.

options.label: 5B Darken text only to 4.5:1
options.description: Keep the pink surface, pick a new darker red. Adds a token DESIGN.md lacks.

questions.question:
D7 — Issue 6: How do InlineStatus text, the error message and the Retry button lay out at 640px and below?
Project/branch/task: main — PLAN.md status area under the header actions, Pass 6 Responsive.
ELI10: After a failed save on a phone, three things want the same 320px-wide row: the status text (“Unsaved changes”), the error message, and a 44px Retry button. The plan specifies the button row at that width but says nothing about this row, so the engineer will pick something and it will probably be a squeezed Retry or a horizontal scroll. The fix is a flex row that wraps: status text and error message stack as text, and Retry sits inline after them when it fits and drops to its own line (left-aligned, 44px tall, auto width) when it doesn't. Above 640px it stays one row.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a Retry button that is too narrow to tap, or the one horizontal scrollbar in a form that promised none, right at the moment the user is already annoyed by a failure.
Recommendation: 6A because it is pure CSS wrapping on the existing InlineStatus container, keeps Retry's 44px target, and never changes DOM or tab order (human: ~30min / CC: ~5min).
Completeness: 6A=10/10, 6B=8/10, 6C=0/10
Pros / cons:
6A) Wrapping flex row: text first, Retry inline when it fits, otherwise on its own left-aligned line at 44px (recommended)
  ✅ Retry keeps a full 44px target at 320px with no horizontal scroll
  ✅ One CSS rule on the existing container; DOM, tab order and live-region boundaries untouched
  ❌ The row height changes when an error appears, so content below shifts down (acceptable: it is below the fold of the action)
6B) Always stack at ≤640px: status text, then error, then a full-width Retry ghost button
  ✅ Predictable layout regardless of message length
  ✅ Matches the full-width Save treatment visually
  ❌ A full-width Retry competes with Save for prominence, and takes a full 44px row even for a short error
6C) Leave unspecified
  ✅ No decision to make now
  ❌ The engineer guesses; most likely outcome is a squeezed Retry or overflow at 320px
Net: 6A wraps only when needed and keeps Retry secondary; 6B is louder and always taller; 6C is the guess.

options.description: Flex-wrap on the status container; Retry 44px, auto width, left-aligned when wrapped. One row above 640px.

options.label: 6B Always stack, full-width Retry
options.description: At ≤640px: status, error, then a full-width Retry ghost button.

questions.question:
D8 — Issue 7: Where does the network/Export/read error message live, and how is it announced?
Project/branch/task: main — PLAN.md status area error message, Pass 7 Unresolved Decisions.
ELI10: When a save fails on the network, the status text stays “Unsaved changes” (so the polite live region announces nothing, because its text didn't change) and an error message appears next to it with Retry. The plan never says whether that message is inside the status live region or its own element with its own announcement. If it's neither, a screen-reader user presses Save, hears nothing, and assumes it worked. Condition: first inspect the existing inline error/retry area; if it already has an announcement role, record that. If it has none, apply the choice below.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a silent failure for screen-reader users, or (if concatenated into the polite region) a delayed announcement that can be interrupted by typing.
Recommendation: 7A because a failure is exactly what role=alert exists for, and keeping it outside the status region preserves the accepted rule that status text does not change on failure (human: ~30min / CC: ~5min).
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
7A) Error message is its own element with role=alert, a sibling between the status text and Retry, outside the role=status region (recommended)
  ✅ Announced immediately and once; status region text stays “Unsaved changes” exactly as accepted
  ✅ Retry (aria-label “Retry save” / “Retry export”) remains a sibling outside both regions, as already specified
  ❌ role=alert is assertive and interrupts; must be used only for request failures, never for the dirty-state text
7B) Append the error message inside the existing role=status region after “Unsaved changes”
  ✅ Single live region, simplest DOM, aria-atomic re-reads the combined text
  ✅ Polite announcement never interrupts what the user is doing
  ❌ Changes the status region's text on failure, which the plan says stays “Unsaved changes”; polite announcements can be lost while typing
7C) Leave unspecified
  ✅ No decision now
  ❌ Most likely outcome is a visually present, unannounced error
Net: 7A announces failures reliably without touching the status contract; 7B is simpler but rewrites accepted status text and may be missed; 7C risks silence.

options.label: 7A Own element, role=alert, outside status region (recommended)
options.description: Error message is a sibling between status text and Retry with role=alert. Status text unchanged. Inspect existing area first.

options.label: 7B Inside the role=status region
options.description: Append the error to the polite status region's text after “Unsaved changes”.

options.label: 7C Leave unspecified
options.description: No spec; engineer decides. Gap stays open.

answers.D8 \u2014 Issue 7: Where does the networ: 7A Own element, role=alert, outside status region (recommended)

# Plan: Settings Page UI redesign

Source plan: `PLAN.md` (repo root). Design system: `DESIGN.md` (repo root).
Review: `/plan-design-review`, text-only (mockups skipped at user request),
native voice only (outside voices skipped at user request).

## Context
The account-settings form already exists and matches most of DESIGN.md. This
plan fixes five known inconsistencies between the shipped form and the approved
design system without changing structure, components, or accepted behavior.
Everything under "Existing product and accepted behavior" is carried over
unchanged from `PLAN.md` and is not up for redesign.

## Existing product and accepted behavior (carried over from PLAN.md, unchanged)
This updates an existing account-settings form using the checked-in DESIGN.md.
The shell and components already exist. Profile and Notifications are the only
sections, with visible headings and associated field labels. The page header
contains the title, a short description, and Save/Reset/Cancel/Export actions.
The existing description is “Manage your display name, email address, and notification preferences.”
Preserve that description verbatim.
Preserve the approved single-column structure and component behavior.
The page title “Account settings” is h1. Profile and Notifications are h2
headings that label their fieldsets via aria-labelledby; no heading level is skipped.
The existing DOM and visual order are:
```text
Persistent app navigation
main: Account settings (h1) + description
  Save | Reset | Cancel | Export
  InlineStatus
  Profile (h2): Display name, Email
  Notifications (h2): Weekly digest, Product tips
```

Journey: a user arrives from account navigation wanting to adjust preferences,
edits the labeled fields, saves, and reads the inline Saved timestamp before
leaving. The feedback preserves confidence that their preferences were stored.
The persistent InlineStatus has role=status, aria-live=polite, aria-atomic=true.
After success it reads “Saved at HH:mm” in the user’s local 24-hour time.
Editing away from a saved value changes its text to “Unsaved changes”, so
dirty state never relies on color or the Save button being enabled. Reverting
all edits or confirming Reset restores the last successful save timestamp.
Before any successful save, unchanged values show blank status text; editing
shows “Unsaved changes”, and reverting or confirming Reset restores blank text.
Failed saves retain “Unsaved changes” alongside the error message.
Initial loading uses the existing form skeleton. A new account sees useful
default preferences as specified in DESIGN.md rather than an empty page. Read failures show Retry.
Save is atomic: all fields persist together or none do, so partial success is
not exposed. Field validation, network failure, and successful-save feedback
use the exact existing DESIGN.md patterns. Preserve unsaved values after errors.
Disable repeat Save submissions while pending. Save and Export are mutually
exclusive: disable both while either is pending. After Save finishes, Export
downloads the latest successfully saved preferences. Reset restores saved values only
after confirmation; Cancel confirms discarding dirty edits before returning to
the previous page; Export downloads the current saved preferences as JSON.
Reset and Cancel are disabled while Save or Export is pending; all four header
actions return to their idle/dirty-state behavior when it settles. While preparing Export, use the existing inline
spinner beside “Exporting…” inside its disabled button, aria-busy=true, with reduced-motion support.
An Export failure uses the existing inline error/retry area and preserves
unsaved fields. Retry repeats Export; success clears only that Export error.
Retry controls are siblings beside the status text, outside its live region.
Visible text stays “Retry”; its aria-label is “Retry save” or “Retry export” for that operation.
The read-failure control follows the same pattern with aria-label “Retry loading”.
The existing router protects dirty edits on every in-app exit, including
persistent app navigation, using the same Cancel confirmation dialog.
Register the browser-native beforeunload warning only while the form is dirty;
remove it when clean. Confirmed in-app navigation uses the existing destination
heading focus behavior; Keep editing returns focus to the attempted exit.
During Save or Export, both request buttons use aria-disabled=true plus an
explicit click/keyboard activation guard, rather than the HTML disabled attribute.
They remain focusable and keep the existing disabled appearance. Reset and
Cancel use HTML disabled during the request. Do not move focus while pending
or after success. On a network error, focus the operation-specific Retry only
if focus is still on the request trigger; never steal focus the user moved.
The existing InlineStatus text stays unchanged while Save is pending:
Unsaved changes for a dirty form, otherwise its saved timestamp or initial
blank text. Pending feedback belongs to the request button; do not repeat
Saving… in the status live region. Success and failure use the outcomes above.
When clean and idle, Reset is disabled because it has nothing to discard,
and Cancel navigates back immediately without a confirmation. When dirty
and idle, Reset and Cancel use their existing discard confirmations. Their
44px geometry is unchanged; the disabled style is separate from pending feedback.

Responsive behavior: above 640px keep the header action group in one row; at
640px and below, place full-width Save first and the three secondary actions
in one equal-column row below it, preserving DOM/tab order. The form fits 320px
without horizontal scroll, including the secondary actions and their 44px targets.
All controls have visible focus rings and 44px targets. Use semantic fieldsets,
labels, a main landmark and heading order; errors link through aria-describedby.
Focus-visible on every control and dialog action is the existing 2px solid
#1d4ed8 outline, offset 2px on white, with measured contrast above 3:1.
Dialogs trap focus; Escape cancels. Closing while staying on the form restores
focus to the Reset or Cancel trigger. Confirmed navigation uses the existing
destination-main-heading focus behavior. Export remains a
clearly labeled button. Respect reduced motion. No additional visual exploration
or component replacement is part of this established form update.
Retain the existing system-ui, sans-serif font family, including on form controls.

## Known gaps (from PLAN.md) — PENDING review decisions
Each item below is an unresolved review finding. DESIGN.md prescribes a token
for each, but that is a proposed fix, not an approved change. Nothing here
moves into implementation tasks until it gets its own decision in the review.

| # | Gap (from PLAN.md) | Proposed fix (DESIGN.md token) | Status |
|---|--------------------|--------------------------------|--------|
| G1 | Visual hierarchy: Save looks identical to Reset/Cancel/Export | Save = only filled primary (#1d4ed8, white text); Reset/Cancel/Export = neutral ghost | APPROVED (D3 → 1A) |
| G2 | Spacing: 16/24/32px mixed between sections | 8px base: sections 32px, field groups 24px, label-to-input 8px | APPROVED (D7 → 5A) |
| G3 | Color: error red on pink at ~3:1 | error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2 + icon + explicit text (AA) | APPROVED (D5 → 3A) |

## Approved design decisions (from this review)

### A1. Action group hierarchy (G1, approved D3 → 1A)
Save is the only filled primary action: background #1d4ed8, white text, using
the existing Button primary variant. Reset, Cancel, and Export use the existing
neutral ghost variant. No change to labels, order (Save | Reset | Cancel |
Export), DOM/tab order, 44px geometry, or the disabled/pending appearance rules
already accepted above. The existing 2px #1d4ed8 focus ring applies to all four.
Verify: at >640px the filled Save is the single highest-contrast element in the
action row; at 640px and below the full-width filled Save sits above the three
ghost buttons in one equal-column row.

### A2. Save pending state (G5, approved D4 → 2A)
While the Save request is in flight, the Save button shows the existing inline
spinner beside the label “Saving…”, with aria-disabled=true, aria-busy=true, and
the explicit click/keyboard activation guard already accepted above. The
spinner respects prefers-reduced-motion using the existing spinner's
reduced-motion mode (static indicator, no rotation). The button keeps its
44px geometry and the existing disabled appearance; set a min-width on Save so
the label change from “Save” to “Saving…” does not reflow the action row.
InlineStatus text does not change while pending (accepted rule). On settle,
the label returns to “Save” and the outcome is shown through the accepted
success/failure patterns. This is the same pattern Export already uses with
“Exporting…”.
Verify: throttle the network to 3s; on click, Save reads “Saving…” with the
spinner within one frame, repeat clicks and Enter/Space are ignored, Export/
Reset/Cancel are disabled, focus stays on Save, and with reduced motion enabled
the spinner does not animate.

### A3. Error color and presentation (G3, approved D5 → 3A)
All error surfaces on this form (inline field errors, ErrorSummary, the
network/read/export error area beside InlineStatus) use error.text #991b1b on
error.surface #fef2f2 (measured contrast ≈7.4:1, above WCAG AA 4.5:1), with the
existing error icon and explicit message text so status is never communicated
by color alone. Field errors keep their aria-describedby link; the summary
keeps its links to each invalid field. No layout or copy changes.
Verify: measure text/surface contrast with a contrast checker (≥4.5:1); confirm
the icon renders with the message in inline, summary, and status-area errors;
confirm a grayscale screenshot still reads as an error via icon and text.

### A4. Typography roles (G4, approved D6 → 4A)
Two type roles only, per DESIGN.md: 16px for body, field labels, helper text,
input values, switch labels, InlineStatus, error text, and button labels; 20px
for the Profile and Notifications h2 headings. Remove the 14px and 18px label
sizes. The h1 keeps its existing app-level size. Font family stays
system-ui, sans-serif, inherited by form controls (accepted, not changed here).
Verify: computed font-size on every label, helper, status, error, and button is
16px; both h2 elements are 20px; no element on the form computes below 16px.

### A5. Spacing rhythm (G2, approved D7 → 5A)
One 8px-based scale with three named gaps, per DESIGN.md:
- section gap 32px: description → action group, action group → InlineStatus,
  InlineStatus → Profile fieldset, Profile fieldset → Notifications fieldset;
- field-group gap 24px: between fields inside a fieldset (Display name → Email;
  Weekly digest → Product tips), and h2 → first field;
- label-to-input gap 8px: label → its input/switch; helper or error text sits
  8px below the control.
Replace the ad-hoc 16px and off-scale gaps; no other layout change. At 640px
and below, the 8px scale also governs the gap between full-width Save and the
secondary-action row (use 8px) and between the three secondary buttons (8px),
which keeps 44px targets inside 320px.
Verify: measure computed margins/gaps in dev tools at 1024px and 320px; every
vertical gap on the form is 8, 24, or 32px; the 320px layout has no horizontal
scroll.
